column3: The Hebrew explicitly says “the king,” where BSB uses “he.” It says “curtain,” where BSB uses “tent.”
The Hebrew says “in a tent and in a tabernacle”; BSB combines these as “with a tent as My dwelling.”
The Hebrew says “tribes of Israel”; BSB uses “leaders.”
The Hebrew says “a great name”; BSB says “a name.”
The Hebrew treats “My people Israel” as singular in the following pronouns and verbs; BSB uses plural forms.
The Hebrew repeats “the LORD”; BSB replaces the second occurrence with “He Himself.”
The Hebrew uses “seed” for the descendant and says “lie down” with the fathers; BSB uses “descendant” and “rest.”
The Hebrew says that His loving devotion will not depart; BSB expresses this passively as not being removed.
The Hebrew says “before you”; BSB says “before Me.”
The Hebrew distinguishes “all these words” and “all this vision”; BSB combines them as “all the words of this vision.”
The Hebrew uses the word “instruction” or “law” of man; BSB renders it as “custom with man.”
The Hebrew says “all this greatness” and describes making it known to the servant as a purpose; BSB says “this great thing” and states that it has been revealed.
The Hebrew uses the images of uncovering the servant’s ear and finding his heart; BSB uses “revealed” and “found the courage.”
